prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1387; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and said a neck strain developed afterward. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and is handling the claim directly.

Entry 2: The police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver gave an account of the collision that matches the claimant's.

Entry 3: Scene photos show damage consistent with the described impact, and the repair estimate lines up with the force of a crash of this kind. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 4: Claimant has told the same account of events in every conversation so far. The reported neck injury fits the kind and force of this impact.

Entry 5: A neighbor believes the car was damaged some weeks before the reported collision. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, so this needs follow-up.

Entry 6: No earlier injury to the neck or upper back is known from the records checked so far. Treatment has run somewhat longer than usual for this type of injury.

Entry 7: The neighbor's report is being reviewed alongside the vehicle history and treatment timeline before any decision is made.
